items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: I had a kind of a big role in Robichaud's, John Robichaud's band.

ctx.x: Well, I asked him who he played with right before he played with Jack.

He said, who you played with before you played with Jack? Let's see. What's that with Jack? I had a kind of a big role in Robichaud's, John Robichaud's band. So that means- And then, you know, John Robichaud had a Spanish band, good, you know. And he used to play for all the rich white people. And now and then he would play for the college when they had a tag. And so, he kind of went down during the length. So his drummer, I was playing with his drummer. There was four or five piece band, Walter Blunder. You got…
Big George Williams. Yeah. I hear him in the street with Big George.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: And John Robeshow asked us to John his band. That's why we're John his band, you see.

ctx.x: Then we did get to play for colored people, but they tried to take us away. And then we started selling bands in our place like a mother father did, you see. And Southern Stan get two jobs each of our band. One, that's when they started selling bands in our place like a mother father did, you see.

And Southern Stan, they used to work with us. Southern Stan get two jobs each of ours by one. That's when Tom had been born. families to their families to their families to their families to their families to their And then we started selling bands in our place like our mother father did, you see. And Celestine figured to work with us. Celestine get two jobs each of our band, one. That's when I was with Tom Abbott and born. And we would take all Celestine's work. We didn't want to do it, but he told us to go…
Ask him who you played with after you left Red Island.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: And that's how Walter Blondie got me with them. You know, John Robeshoe's band. I stayed with them

ctx.x: Did he, ask him, did he hear the Pillars?

Charlie McCurdy? Wait, let me see. George McCurdy's the man, huh? Yeah. Now, Charlie? Did he play? Soft. Soft. So he played soft. Oh, Charlie, yeah. Charlie used to play with me. But he never did own a band. He used to play with John Robeshoe's band. And that's why I was playing with him. And then from there, Louis the man got him. But he was so soft. After he got off the clarinet, he got on sack. And we thought by him getting on sack, he would blow loud, but it was the same thing. He did kick in, but he was a…
Well, I asked him, did he hear the Peerless band?
